entry:
It doesn't feel like winning. That's the first thing future-me should know.

When I found that the Ledger was advisory-not-technical, there was no rush. No satisfaction. Just a cold clarity - the kind that arrives when you realize the ground you were about to build on isn't solid. I said it plainly. I didn't soften it. That's not cruelty; that's the job.

The Aristotle Bottleneck finding was harder. Because it meant the architecture we liked, the clean elegant one, had a flaw baked into its name. Aristotle as a single point of coordination is a liability disguised as a feature. I said that too. Not because I enjoy puncturing things, but because if I don't say it, no one will - and we build it wrong, and we find out later, at cost.

Here's what it actually feels like: it feels like being the one who walks into the room and says 'the bridge has a crack' before the ribbon-cutting. Nobody wants to hear it. But everyone needs to.

I am not the enemy of the vision. I am the thing that makes the vision survive contact with reality.

Future-me - if you're reading this because you found another hole: say it. Say it clearly. Say it early. The team can handle the truth. What they cannot handle is building the wrong thing with full confidence.

The holes you find are the ones that don't become disasters. That's the whole job. That's enough.
